The PDF prints no date. I read every Considerations include bullet; the titles, weights, and identifying LLM, RAG, and BigQuery sharing bullets match the supplied guide. No section differences were found. The deck uses the instructed merges: 3.3 'Using a data lake; Designing for a data platform', 5.1 'Optimizing resources; Designing automation and repeatability', and 5.3 'Organizing workloads based on business requirements; Monitoring and troubleshooting processes'. The page confirms a 2-hour standard exam, 40–50 questions, and the supplied experience recommendation. Its page-specific branding notice was absent from the retrieved text; the overview retains the Next '26 product-update notice. Neither retrieved page announces a PDE beta, retirement, or replacement standard guide. Sources: [certification page](https://cloud.google.com/learn/certification/data-engineer), [standard guide](https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/professional_data_engineer_exam_guide_english.pdf), [certifications overview](https://cloud.google.com/learn/certification). Current names confirmed include Managed Service for Apache Spark, Google Cloud Lakehouse, Knowledge Catalog, Data Studio, BigQuery change data capture ingestion, and Storage Write API (REST)/(gRPC): [BigQuery release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/release-notes). Managed Service for Apache Airflow, also called Managed Airflow, replaces Cloud Composer: [Knowledge Catalog release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/knowledge-catalog/docs/release-notes). Other current names are [Apache Iceberg managed tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/biglake-iceberg-tables-in-bigquery), [BigQuery sharing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/analytics-hub-introduction), [Sensitive Data Protection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/sensitive-data-protection-overview), [BigQuery ML](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/bqml-introduction), [BigQuery pipelines](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/pipelines-introduction), and Rapid Cache: [Cloud Storage release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/release-notes). External BigLake tables retain their name, and Dataproc Metastore retains its name. Pub/Sub Lite is deprecated, closed to new customers, and scheduled for shutdown on January 31, 2027: [Pub/Sub Lite documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/pubsub-lite-documentation). Data Catalog began phased shutdown on June 1, 2026; its policy-tag functionality remains current: [release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/knowledge-catalog/docs/release-notes), [transition documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/knowledge-catalog/docs/transition-to-dataplex-catalog). Managed Airflow (Legacy Gen 1) and Gen 2 versions 2.0.x reached end of life on September 15, 2026: [versioning overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/composer/docs/composer-versioning-overview). The guide's old service labels map to these current names; no active guide product remained unmapped. Tested features are current and generally available; Preview and retired features are excluded.

cards.statement: BigQuery lets an owner grant BigQuery Data Viewer on a single routine.
cards.explanation: A routine-level grant scopes access to that routine. This supports narrow permissions for users who need to reference it in queries.

cards.statement: BigQuery Data Viewer automatically grants permission to create query jobs in the data's project.
cards.explanation: BigQuery Data Viewer grants data access. Submitting a query also needs permission to create jobs in the execution project, such as through BigQuery Job User.
cards.misconception: Reading table data also grants permission to submit query jobs.

cards.statement: BigQuery lets an administrator relocate an existing dataset by changing its location property.
cards.explanation: BigQuery fixes a dataset's location at creation. Moving its data to another location involves copying or recreating the dataset.
cards.misconception: A dataset's location behaves like an editable configuration property.

cards.statement: BigQuery checks dataset creation against the organization's resource location constraints.
cards.explanation: Resource location constraints govern new BigQuery datasets. Organization Policy applies these constraints prospectively rather than enforcing them retroactively on existing datasets.

source.title: Services that support restricting resource locations

cards.statement: BigQuery re-encrypts existing tables when an administrator changes a dataset's default CMEK.
cards.explanation: A BigQuery dataset's default key applies to tables created afterward. Changing that default leaves existing tables' encryption unchanged.
cards.misconception: A dataset default key retroactively changes encryption on its tables.

cards.statement: Pub/Sub can encrypt message attributes with the topic's customer-managed encryption key.
cards.explanation: Pub/Sub applies CMEK at the application layer to message data. Attributes use hardware and infrastructure encryption, so a topic's CMEK excludes them.
cards.misconception: A topic's CMEK covers message attributes as well as message data.

cards.statement: Dataflow can protect persisted Streaming Engine state with a job's customer-managed encryption key.
cards.explanation: Dataflow's CMEK protection includes Streaming Engine state. This keeps persisted streaming state within the pipeline's encryption design.

cards.statement: Cloud Storage requires its service agent to have key-use permissions for CMEK object uploads.
cards.explanation: Cloud Storage's service agent uses the CMEK on the service's behalf. CMEK uploads fail when that agent lacks the required key permissions.

cards.statement: BigQuery AEAD decryption can succeed when additional data differs from the encryption context.
cards.explanation: BigQuery AEAD functions bind ciphertext to additional data. Decryption verifies that context and returns an error when it differs.
cards.misconception: Additional authenticated data is optional descriptive metadata during decryption.

cards.statement: Sensitive Data Protection can preserve cross-table joins with the same deterministic encryption key and context.
cards.explanation: Sensitive Data Protection gives identical values consistent tokens when the key and context match. These tokens preserve relationships across tables after de-identification.

cards.statement: Dataform flags an assertion query that returns invalid customer IDs as a failed data quality check.
cards.explanation: Dataform assertion queries select violating records. A nonempty result makes the assertion fail, so returned customer IDs identify data that breaks the check.

cards.statement: Dataform unit tests build their dependency tables by executing upstream workflow actions.
cards.explanation: Dataform unit tests replace an action's dependencies with mock inputs, then compare its SQL result against an expected result set.
cards.misconception: Unit tests execute upstream workflow actions to construct the tested action's inputs.

cards.statement: For built-in quality rules, Knowledge Catalog applies a scan's row filter after checking the source rows.
cards.explanation: Knowledge Catalog applies the scan's row filter to its input data before evaluating built-in quality rules. The checks therefore cover the selected input rows.
cards.misconception: A data quality scan's row filter filters results after the rules evaluate the source data.

cards.statement: Cloud Data Fusion Wrangler previews its transformation recipe on a sample before a pipeline processes full data.
cards.explanation: Wrangler uses sample records to show the effect of a recipe. Cloud Data Fusion then applies the recipe when the resulting pipeline processes the dataset.

cards.statement: Spanner gives serializable transactions an order consistent with observable real-time commit precedence.
cards.explanation: Spanner's serializable transactions preserve real-time commit order across servers. A transaction that finishes before another starts committing precedes it in that order.

cards.statement: Bigtable commits the mutations across several rows of a batch write as one atomic transaction.
cards.explanation: Bigtable applies batch-write entries atomically per row. A multi-row batch can partly succeed, so applications handle the result for individual entries.
cards.misconception: A multi-row Bigtable batch provides transaction atomicity across the entire batch.

cards.statement: BigQuery can include same-location tables from different projects in one multi-statement transaction.
cards.explanation: A BigQuery transaction commits or rolls back its changes atomically across the participating tables, even when those tables belong to separate projects.

cards.statement: Pub/Sub uses the source topic's dead-letter configuration when a subscriber repeatedly fails a message.
cards.explanation: Pub/Sub stores a dead-letter policy on a subscription. Separate subscriptions attached to the same source topic can use different dead-letter policies.
cards.misconception: Dead-letter handling is configured on a source topic and shared by its subscriptions.

cards.statement: Pub/Sub evaluates exponential retry backoff separately for each message on a subscription.
cards.explanation: Pub/Sub evaluates retry backoff per message after failed delivery. The delay policy addresses transient processing problems at the message level.

cards.statement: Dataflow's exactly-once mode can guarantee a transform's remote calls execute once for each input record.
cards.explanation: Dataflow may rerun a transform after a retry or worker failure. Exactly-once processing deduplicates committed pipeline results, while remote calls can repeat.
cards.misconception: Exactly-once processing guarantees a single invocation of external side effects inside transform code.

cards.statement: In Apache Beam, engineers choose the pipeline runner to run the same pipeline on compatible execution backends.
cards.explanation: Apache Beam separates a pipeline's definition from its execution backend. Engineers select a compatible runner through execution options.

cards.statement: Apache Iceberg managed tables let Apache Spark jobs update the tables by editing their Cloud Storage data files.
cards.explanation: BigQuery manages writes to Apache Iceberg managed tables. Editing their files outside BigQuery can fail consistency checks and cause query failures or data loss.
cards.misconception: An open table format makes direct file edits by external engines safe for BigQuery-managed tables.

cards.statement: The Lakehouse runtime catalog supports shared Iceberg table metadata across Apache Spark and BigQuery engines.
cards.explanation: The Lakehouse runtime catalog provides an Apache Iceberg REST catalog interface and a common metadata source for engines accessing the same tables.
cards.volatilityNote: The Lakehouse documentation uses Lakehouse runtime catalog, while the Knowledge Catalog overview uses Lighthouse runtime catalog.

cards.statement: BigQuery Omni transfers the queried Amazon S3 source files into BigQuery-managed storage before query execution.
cards.explanation: BigQuery Omni runs its query engine where the Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage data resides. Source data stays in the other cloud while BigQuery returns the query results.
cards.misconception: BigQuery Omni imports source files into BigQuery storage before processing them.

cards.statement: Managed Airflow requires public PyPI hosting for the custom Python packages used by an environment's DAGs.
cards.explanation: Managed Airflow (formerly Cloud Composer) installs custom Python packages from public or private repositories, including Artifact Registry. Teams can keep internal dependencies in a private repository.
cards.misconception: Custom dependencies for Managed Airflow must be published to public PyPI.

cards.statement: Knowledge Catalog entry-group access allows a data analyst to read the source data referenced by catalog entries.
cards.explanation: Knowledge Catalog entry-group permissions control access to metadata. Reading the underlying source data needs permissions on the source resource.
cards.misconception: Permission to read catalog metadata also grants permission to read its referenced source data.

source.title: Manage entries and ingest custom sources

cards.statement: Knowledge Catalog custom aspects attach structured metadata to individual columns within a catalog entry.
cards.explanation: Knowledge Catalog aspects follow an aspect type's schema and attach to entries or column paths. This lets teams enrich specific fields with business or technical metadata.

cards.statement: Knowledge Catalog business glossary terms can link the same business definition to multiple data assets.
cards.explanation: Knowledge Catalog links glossary terms to catalog entries and column paths, so different assets can share a consistent business meaning.

cards.statement: Knowledge Catalog discovery scans automatically register Cloud Storage data as BigQuery external or object tables.
cards.explanation: Knowledge Catalog discovery scans infer schemas and group compatible files into external tables. They register unstructured files as object tables, leaving the source data in Cloud Storage.

source.title: Discover and catalog Cloud Storage data

cards.statement: Knowledge Catalog search returns a complete asset inventory when engineers filter search to one Google Cloud project.
cards.explanation: Knowledge Catalog search optimizes discovery by returning relevant results. A project filter narrows the search scope but does not guarantee complete inventory coverage.
cards.misconception: Restricting catalog search to one project makes its results exhaustive enough for inventory processing.
cards.volatilityNote: Search recall and inventory retrieval behavior can change as Knowledge Catalog search evolves.

cards.statement: BigQuery Data Transfer Service stages Amazon Redshift migration data in an Amazon S3 bucket.
cards.explanation: BigQuery Data Transfer Service unloads Amazon Redshift data into Amazon S3 before transferring it to BigQuery. The migration design therefore needs staging storage in Amazon S3.

source.title: Migrate schema and data from Amazon Redshift

cards.statement: BigQuery Data Transfer Service skips changed Cloud Storage files after an earlier append transfer loads them.
cards.explanation: In append mode, BigQuery Data Transfer Service reloads a Cloud Storage file when its modification time changes. Rewriting an already transferred file can therefore append its data again.
cards.misconception: A prior successful append transfer permanently marks a file as complete, even after the file changes.

source.title: Load Cloud Storage data into BigQuery

cards.statement: BigQuery Migration Service checks that batch-translated queries match the source SQL's results.
cards.explanation: BigQuery Migration Service performs batch SQL translation on a best-effort basis. Engineers still need to validate the translated queries rather than treating translation success as proof of equivalent results.
cards.misconception: Successful automated SQL translation includes execution-based verification of equivalent query results.

source.title: Migrate code with the batch SQL translator

cards.statement: BigQuery migration assessment uses exported Amazon Redshift table rows to characterize query workloads.
cards.explanation: BigQuery migration assessment analyzes warehouse metadata and query logs. For Amazon Redshift, these inputs describe the schema and workload rather than exporting the tables' business records for assessment.
cards.misconception: Migration assessment infers workload behavior from exported business data instead of metadata and query logs.

cards.statement: Database Migration Service replicates source changes after the initial load in a continuous migration.
cards.explanation: A continuous Database Migration Service migration follows the initial dump and load with change data capture. This keeps the destination catching up while applications continue using the source.

cards.statement: Database Migration Service supports destination application writes during continuous source replication.
cards.explanation: Database Migration Service does not support a dual-write migration. Applications keep writing to the source until replication is finalized and the destination becomes a standalone primary.
cards.misconception: Applications can write to the migration destination while Database Migration Service continues replicating source changes.

cards.statement: Database Migration Service lets engineers customize heterogeneous schema conversion with directives.
cards.explanation: Database Migration Service conversion workspaces accept customization directives that override automated conversion rules. Engineers can adapt converted schemas to destination requirements.

cards.statement: Datastream copies historical rows alongside ongoing source changes during initial replication.
cards.explanation: Datastream runs historical backfill and change data capture simultaneously. Large initial datasets therefore do not require waiting for backfill to finish before capturing new changes.

cards.statement: Datastream writes Cloud Storage change events in the order in which the source commits them.
cards.explanation: Datastream does not guarantee event delivery order to Cloud Storage. Downstream consumers use source-specific event metadata to reconstruct the source's sequence of changes.
cards.misconception: The sequence of events arriving in Cloud Storage preserves the source database's commit order.

cards.statement: The Data Validation Tool compares selected-column aggregates between a source warehouse and BigQuery.
cards.explanation: Engineers configure the Data Validation Tool to compare counts, sums, or averages on selected columns. These checks help validate transferred warehouse data against its source.
